```{r setup, include=FALSE}

library(catcheR); library(knitr)
OUT <- params$output
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
show <- function(f) {
  p <- file.path(OUT, f)
  if (file.exists(p)) knitr::include_graphics(p) else invisible(NULL)
}
```

# What this document does

It puts one 10x, one PIPseq and one Parse run side by side. It does **not**
re-read any FASTQ: every number comes from the objects the three entry points
already wrote, so the whole document knits in seconds.

Run the three pipelines first — each writes `<chemistry>catch_<sample>.rds`
into its own `Output/<chemistry>/`:

```r
rmarkdown::render(system.file("rmd", "catcheR_tenxcatch_analysis_EB.Rmd", package = "catcheR"),
                  params = list(analysis_dir = "analysis_EB_10X",   sample_name = "AB019a"))
rmarkdown::render(system.file("rmd", "catcheR_pipcatch_analysis_EB.Rmd", package = "catcheR"),
                  params = list(analysis_dir = "analysis_EB_PIP",   sample_name = "AB019b"))
rmarkdown::render(system.file("rmd", "catcheR_parsecatch_analysis_EB.Rmd", package = "catcheR"),
                  params = list(analysis_dir = "analysis_EB_PARSE", sample_name = "AB019c"))
```

Then knit this one. Add or drop a chemistry by editing the lists in the chunk
below — nothing else assumes there are exactly three.

# Inputs

```{r inputs}
# Each entry point writes into Output/<chemistry>/ (its `subdir` default), so
# the three pipelines cannot overwrite each other. Older runs used a flat
# Output/, so fall back to that when the nested file is absent.
find_rds <- function(dir, chem, sample) {
  f <- file.path(dir, "Output", chem, sprintf("%s_%s.rds", chem, sample))
  if (file.exists(f)) return(f)
  file.path(dir, "Output", sprintf("%s_%s.rds", chem, sample))
}
rds <- c(find_rds(params$tenx_dir,  "tenxcatch",  params$tenx_sample),
         find_rds(params$pip_dir,   "pipcatch",   params$pip_sample),
         find_rds(params$parse_dir, "parsecatch", params$parse_sample))
cal <- c(
  file.path(params$tenx_dir,  "scratch", params$tenx_called),
  file.path(params$pip_dir,   "scratch", params$pip_called),
  file.path(params$parse_dir, "scratch", params$parse_called))
names(rds) <- names(cal) <- unlist(params$labels)

inv <- data.frame(
  chemistry = names(rds),
  run_object = basename(rds), object_found = file.exists(rds),
  called_cells = basename(cal), called_found = file.exists(cal))
stopifnot(all(inv$object_found))
kable(inv, caption = "Run objects and called-cell lists")
```

The called-cell lists are what make the comparison fair. Each chemistry's own
preprocessing (Cell Ranger, PIPseeker, split-pipe) decides which barcodes are
cells; counting against the barcodes catcheR merely *observed* would include
the ambient floor and inflate coverage — on the Parse library by more than
tenfold.

# The comparison

```{r compare}
C <- catcheR_compare_chemistries(as.list(rds), called = cal,
                                 output_dir = OUT, verbose = FALSE)
kable(C[, c("chemistry", "pipeline", "read_pairs", "pct_cellbc", "pct_assigned",
            "called_cells", "called_one_clone", "pct_called_one_clone",
            "median_depth_called", "constructs", "clones")],
      caption = "One row per chemistry; percentages are of that library's own read pairs")
```

```{r fig, fig.cap="Barcode yield across chemistries"}
show("chemistry_comparison.png")
```

# How to read it

**Panel A — where the reads go.** Each stage is a strict subset of the one
above, and the axis is logarithmic because the libraries can differ by three
orders of magnitude in the share of reads that reach a barcode. A library that
collapses at *cell barcode parsed* has an amplicon problem upstream of
anything catcheR does: a primer-dimer product carries no capture oligo, so its
read 2 (10x, PIPseq) or read 1 (Parse) is adapter read-through rather than a
barcode.

**Panel B — the only denominator that compares.** Cells the platform called,
split into those resolving to exactly one clone and everything else. This is
the number to put in a methods section.

**Panel C — depth, with a caveat.** A chemistry whose molecular index is long
enough to deduplicate reports *molecules*; one whose index is too short reports
*reads*. The `umi_dedup` column says which, and the panel subtitle names the
read-counted runs. Do not quote the two as one number.

```{r dedup}
kable(C[, c("chemistry", "umi_dedup", "events", "median_depth_called")],
      caption = "umi_dedup = FALSE means `events` are reads, not molecules")
```
